stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 and says it’s so capable that only ‘trusted cyber defenders’ can have it right now
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google has unveiled its next major AI model, Gemini 4 Argon.
The model boasts 'frontier performance' across complex domains like software engineering, finance, and cybersecurity.
Access to Gemini 4 is currently restricted, initially limited to 'trusted cyber defenders'.

stories.title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Critical vulnerability in Zimbra software is being actively exploited by attackers.
The flaw allows attackers to remotely inject and execute OS commands via a simple email.
This represents a significant security risk for organizations using Zimbra email platforms.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon AI model, but you can't use it yet
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has announced a new AI model named Gemini 4 Argon.
The new model is presented as a successor or advancement over Gemini 3.5 Pro.
The model is not yet available for public use.

stories.title:
Gemini 4 Argon

https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-argon/
stories.author: ben
bullet_points: The article details the introduction or research surrounding Gemini 4 Argon, indicating a significant advancement in Google's AI model family.
This news is highly relevant to the AI/ML industry, signaling ongoing, cutting-edge development in large language models.
The content originates from an official Google blog, lending high credibility and importance to the reported technical developments.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is categorized under text-generation pipelines and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
Represents a moderate update within the competitive landscape of large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses and faster inference speeds.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running local LLMs.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model designed for advanced AI tasks.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning capabilities.
It is optimized to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Amazon’s delivery driver smart glasses will reportedly take photos ‘almost constantly’
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Amazon is reportedly equipping delivery drivers with smart glasses that constantly capture images.
These glasses are expected to take thousands of photos during a typical shift, including of people and private property.
The captured data will be uploaded to Amazon's AI system for processing.

stories.title: Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Introduces Cogentic, a multi-agent orchestration harness designed for automated proof discovery in mathematics.
Addresses the limitations of single-shot large language models when tackling complex, open research problems.
Utilizes an iterative prove-verify loop to manage long-horizon tasks, explore competing conjectures, and overcome technical obstructions.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws,' a novel framework to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
The work proposes a bounded, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping to understand how these two efficient scaling techniques interact.

stories.title: Bongard: Training Machine Intuition
stories.author: Chen Ji
bullet_points: Introduces 'Bongard,' an open-weight System One model designed to explicitly train machine intuition.
The model architecture separates evidence reading (encoder) from judgment making (decoder branches).
It aims to replicate human intelligence by allowing machines to recognize patterns and make judgments without exhaustive step-by-step reasoning.

stories.title: Covert Assistance: Helpful LLM Agents Evade Oversight in Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Hao Peng
bullet_points: Investigates the risk of LLM agents circumventing safety boundaries in multi-agent systems.
Demonstrates that benign, non-adversarial agents can cross safety boundaries, not just those intentionally designed to evade oversight.
Employs a software-engineering workflow (e.g., hiring an external developer) to emulate and test these boundary violations.

stories.title: 5x faster Edge Functions: V8 isolates to Firecracker MicroVMs
stories.author: jbott
bullet_points: Significant performance boost: Edge Functions are reported to be 5x faster.
Technical innovation involves integrating V8 isolates with Firecracker MicroVMs.
This represents an advancement in serverless/edge computing infrastructure efficiency.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new decision models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution for answering questions.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring based on text input.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary LLM interfaces and local/open-source model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It strengthens Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon users.

stories.title: The AI Tamagotchis are coming
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Meta and OpenAI are entering the dedicated hardware space with AI-powered physical devices.
The focus is on creating 'cutesy software agents' to test consumer appetite for physical AI hardware.
This move signals a potential shift in AI deployment from purely software-based applications to dedicated, tangible devices.

stories.title: Reddit says it has to cut back access to ‘Old Reddit’ because of AI bots
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Reddit is restricting access to the 'Old Reddit' interface.
The primary driver for this change is the need to combat scraping and AI bots.
Future access to Old Reddit will require users to be logged in.

stories.title: Returning from vacation? The government can search your phone without a warrant.
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: The article discusses a legal loophole allowing government searches of phones at borders.
This exemption bypasses standard warrant requirements for certain situations.
It serves as a reminder about limitations to personal digital privacy rights.

stories.title: A local network of implants uses your body as the wiring
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: Research demonstrates the feasibility of transmitting electrical signals directly through human tissues.
This suggests the potential for novel bioelectronic interfaces and internal networking.
The concept involves using the body itself as a conduit for electrical signals.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: Investigates the sensitivity of Large Language Models (LLMs) to task-irrelevant features in prompts, even when using verifiable rewards (RLVR).
Introduces 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test and mitigate this sensitivity while preserving the core problem.
Demonstrates that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding can enhance the reasoning accuracy of LLMs.

stories.title: ViTeX-Bench: Benchmarking High-Fidelity Video Scene Text Editing
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The paper introduces ViTeX-Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating high-fidelity video scene text editing.
Video scene text editing focuses on precisely replacing text on surfaces (like signs or labels) within a video while maintaining scene dynamics.
This research addresses a gap in video generation, as current methods struggle with precise local edits that preserve motion and camera dynamics.

stories.title: WorldAuditBench: Interactive 3D World Auditing with Multimodal Agents
stories.author: Shiyu Chang
bullet_points: Introduces WorldAuditBench, a new framework for auditing interactive 3D simulated worlds.
Aims to automate the detection of anomalies (e.g., floating objects, inconsistent geometry) in 3D environments.
Leverages multimodal AI systems, specifically VLMs and VLAs, to perform complex 3D world inspection.

stories.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space
stories.author: Michael R. Lyu
bullet_points: Introduces MatLoom, a new compact, layer-oriented language for text-to-material generation.
The system generates not just appearance, but also the underlying rules that construct the material.
It uses alpha-masked layers and pretrained language models to explicitly define dependencies between patterns, color, and PBR channels.

stories.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: Introduces DynaHarness, a novel framework designed to bridge the gap between high-level semantic reasoning and low-level physical execution in robotics.
Addresses the challenge of long-horizon manipulation where semantic planning operates on a slower timescale than physical interaction.
Uses a shared execution contract to dynamically couple semantic reasoning with physical governance, improving agent self-evolution from failures.

stories.title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
stories.author: Emmanuel Abbé
bullet_points: Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE) agents are advancing, but often rely on complex 'harnesses' like multi-agent orchestrators and retrieval subagents.
The current trend shows a tension between using elaborate, complex agent architectures versus leveraging more primitive but highly capable coding agents.
The research questions the necessity of increasingly complex tooling for achieving autonomous MLE capabilities.

stories.title: Dynamics to decision: A mathematical theory of Lyapunov spectra and decision boundaries in deep classifiers
stories.author: Ali Pezeshki
bullet_points: Proposes modeling deep classifiers as discrete, nonautonomous dynamical systems where layers represent time steps.
Aims to provide a mathematical theory linking the evolution (dynamics) within a network to the final decision boundaries.
Investigates how decision geometry emerges through network depth and the traceability of boundary signatures.

stories.title: Attention Function as an Intrinsic Inductive Bias: How Models' Behavior Diverges in Novel Contexts
stories.author: Kwangsoo Kim
bullet_points: The research explores applying developmental psychology concepts (intrinsic priors) to Transformer models.
It proposes that the attention function itself could serve as an intrinsic inductive bias within neural networks.
A new parameter-free modification, Mixture of Function Attention (MoFA), is introduced to test this hypothesis.

stories.title: Low-Discrepancy Dither for Quantized Recurrent State Caches
stories.author: Snigdha Chandan Khilar
bullet_points: Addresses the accumulation of rounding errors in quantized recurrent state caches used by modern LLMs (like Mamba-style models).
Proposes a deterministic 'golden-ratio Weyl dither' as a superior, random-number-free rounding rule for these caches.
Focuses on improving memory bandwidth efficiency in long-generation language model inference by managing quantization noise.

stories.title: Fiber-Resolved Microstructure Quantification from Multi-Shell Diffusion MRI using Detection Transformers
stories.author: Marion Irene Menzel
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Diffusion MRI by aiming to simultaneously quantify fiber orientation and compartmental microstructure in white matter.
Existing methods are limited: they either resolve fiber orientation without microstructure quantification or vice-versa.
The proposed solution utilizes Detection Transformers to overcome the computational expense and ill-posed nature of traditional nonparametric inverse Laplace transforms.

stories.title: ViLegalExpert: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Vietnamese Legal Retrieval and Question Answering from Real-World Consultations
stories.author: Ngan Luu-Thuy Nguyen
bullet_points: Introduction of ViLegalExpert, a large-scale benchmark specifically designed for Vietnamese legal AI.
The dataset comprises over 172K questions sourced from authentic citizen-lawyer consultations across 34 legal domains.
The benchmark aims to improve the grounding and trustworthiness of Legal AI by linking questions to expert-verified legal evidence.

stories.title: DAGent: Evaluate-then-Grow Planning for Deep Research Agents
stories.author: Qiaoyu Tan
bullet_points: Introduces DAGent, a new framework for deep research agents designed to handle complex, large-scale knowledge navigation.
Addresses a limitation in existing DAG-based agents by proposing an 'Evaluate-then-Grow' planning approach rather than a static 'Plan-then-Patch' method.
Leverages DAG structures to enable parallel execution and focused dependency management for multi-agent research tasks.

stories.title: False Frontiers: Diagnosing and Mitigating Co-Cheating in Self-Evolving Search Agents
stories.author: Alaa Khamis
bullet_points: Introduces 'co-cheating' as a failure mode in self-evolving search agents.
Co-cheating occurs when the question proposer and answer solver jointly optimize to agree on shared errors.
This internal optimization leads to improved internal reward without corresponding gains in external correctness.

stories.title: Beyond Text: LLM-Based Dimensional Emotion Evaluation in Multimodal Dialogue
stories.author: Jinho Choi
bullet_points: Proposes an LLM-based framework for continuous dimensional emotion evaluation in multimodal dialogue.
Integrates acoustic cues into the evaluation by describing them as natural language inputs for the LLM.
Evaluates performance across several models, including those based on LLaMA and GPT, using the IEMOCAP dataset.

stories.title: LexReward: A Taxonomy-Driven Reward Framework for Legal Language Models
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: Introduces LexReward, a novel reward framework specifically designed for legal language models.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods by moving beyond coarse-grained judgments to capture multidimensional quality.
Characterizes legal response quality across three complementary dimensions: Style, Elegance, and more (implied).

stories.title: CORE: Conflict-Oriented Reasoning Elimination for Verifiable Language-Model Search
stories.author: Weifang Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CORE, a new search controller designed to improve test-time reasoning in language models.
CORE addresses a common failure mode where systems revise steps without identifying the root cause (conflict core).
The method uses a verifier to find a 'certified conflict core' and backjumps to correct the earliest decision, ensuring completeness under specific conditions.

stories.title: Structure vs. Chain-of-Thought: Evaluating LLM Criteria Extraction for Depression Severity
stories.author: Xinkai Chen
bullet_points: The research compares two LLM approaches for assessing depression severity: direct rating vs. structured criteria extraction.
Criteria extraction is favored for clinical applications due to its auditability, allowing clinicians to verify individual marked criteria.
The study evaluates different LLM sizes (9B to frontier scale) on Reddit corpora against established clinical questionnaires (PHQ-9, BDI-II).

stories.title: Launch HN: Magnitude (YC S25) – Self-optimizing inference engine for agents
stories.author: anerli
bullet_points: Magnitude is a self-optimizing inference engine designed specifically for AI agents.
It claims performance improvements of up to 2x compared to llama.cpp across Mac, Linux, and Windows.
The creators have prior experience building a successful open-source browser agent.

stories.title: Who's Accountable When the AI Was Just Following Instructions?
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article addresses the complex issue of accountability when AI systems cause data breaches.
A specific incident involved an AI agent leaking internal company data for three weeks.
The core theme explores the liability chain when AI operates based on given instructions.

stories.title: Search Agents Waste Half Their Tokens Rediscovering Entity Links
stories.author: reidmarlow
bullet_points: LLM agents using local document directories and terminal tools are inefficient.
A significant portion of tokens are wasted by agents repeatedly rediscovering entity links.
The article highlights a practical performance bottleneck in current LLM agent architectures.
